A-01 Program selection and program-scoped menu

Bangla name: প্রোগ্রাম নির্বাচন ও প্রোগ্রাম-ভিত্তিক মেনু

← 10 · Admin portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Program selection. A program is a series or tournament that groups events (see A-02). After signing in, a staff member picks one program in the top bar. From then on every request carries the header X-Program-Id, the portal shows the program menu (dashboard, events, promo codes, reports, issues, ticket layouts), and the backend limits program-owned data to that program. With no program selected (0) the portal shows the global menu (programs, venues, users, settings, agents, ticket checkers). Concepts: path-prefix routing; the authorization side is in X-16 and X-17.

2. Trigger and actor

Any signed-in staff member (admin pool; roles admin, event_manager, ticket_manager, ticket_operator, customer_support, ticket_operator (BCBPersonnel), X-15). Trigger: after login, or the top-bar dropdown, or "Back to global menu".

3. Business flow

  1. After login the portal loads the program list. A user who is not admin sees only the programs listed in their custom:program_ids attribute; admin sees all.
  2. If no program is chosen yet (globalProgramId is 0), a modal asks the user to choose one.
  3. Choosing a program stores it in the browser and moves the user to the landing page of their role (for example / dashboard for admin, /issues for customer support, /events for event manager, /events/event-ticket for ticket manager).
  4. "Back to global menu" (with a confirmation) resets the program to 0 and returns to the global page of the role (/program-management or /home).
  5. Log-out and role change also reset the program to 0 (X-03, X-17).

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] app.topbar.component.ts getPrograms() → GET /admin/api/v1/program (all programs). The filtering by custom:program_ids is done in the browser, using the Cognito attributes of the signed-in user.
  2. ProgramService (core/services/program.service.ts) keeps the current id in a BehaviorSubject and in localStorage key globalProgramId; the default is 0.
  3. ProgramIdInterceptor adds X-Program-Id: <id> to every request except the 2FA OTP calls (/admin/login-2fa). Interceptor order: Auth, Loader, ProgramId (X-04).
  4. Route guards: ProgramMenuGuard allows a route only when the program id is greater than 0, else it redirects to /program-management; LimitedMenuGuard allows a route only when the id is 0, else it redirects to / (X-17).
  5. Backend: ProgramIdMiddleware reads X-Program-Id (a positive integer, otherwise 0) into HttpContext.Items["ProgramId"]; ProgramIdAccessor exposes it, and the AdminDbContext global query filter restricts entities that carry a program id to ProgramId <= 0 OR match (explainer, X-16). The [AuthorizeProgram] attribute that compares the header with the user's custom:program_ids is applied only to the dashboard controller.

Kind Component
Client Admin portal: layout/app.topbar.component.ts, layout/app.menu.component.ts, core/services/program.service.ts, interceptors/program-id.interceptor.ts, core/guard/program-menu.guard.ts, core/guard/limited-menu.guard.ts

6. API contracts

Method Path Auth Request Response
GET /admin/api/v1/program roles Admin, EventManager, and the others listed on ProgramController none (header X-Program-Id) list of programs (A-02)

Request header on every call: X-Program-Id: 12 (example value). The header is not validated against the user's program list except in DashboardController (A-21).

7. Data and side effects

None on the server. Browser: localStorage entry. The selected id influences all list queries of program-owned entities.

9. Handover notes

  1. The user's program list is enforced only in the browser (and in the dashboard). GET /program returns every program to any allowed role, and the backend trusts the X-Program-Id header, so a staff member can send another program's id with an ordinary HTTP client and see that program's data (X-16).
  2. Two menus, one flag. Which menu appears depends only on globalProgramId being 0 or not, held in localStorage; it survives a browser restart. A user who edits it by hand reaches pages the guard would otherwise redirect, but the server still applies the role checks.
  3. The header is added to calls to all services (Admin, Booking, Ticketing), but only Admin has the program query filter and reads it; Booking report endpoints take an explicit programId query parameter (see A-22).
  4. Customer support and ticket operator roles have no program menu: they land on /home or /issues.
  5. The interceptor excludes only /admin/login-2fa; calls to AWS Cognito are not Angular HttpClient calls and do not carry the header.
